name: Black Tooth Hovel
summary: Black Tooth Hovel is a sprawling Dark Horde outpost situated in the central plains of the Burning Steppes. Composed of Blackrock orcs, Firegut ogres, and Smolderthorn trolls, it surrounds a solemn, colossal monument commemorating the fallen Supreme Commander of the Alliance, Anduin Lothar.

sections.title: A Stronghold in the Ash
sections.body: Sprawling across the ashen wastes beneath Blackrock Mountain, the camp known historically as the Pillar of Ash houses a formidable gathering of the Dark Horde. Orcs of the Blackrock clan share the grounds with Firegut ogres and Smolderthorn trolls, outfitting their warbands and tending to heavy Blackrock war kodos. While named in remembrance of the old Black Tooth Grin clan, the settlement serves as a logistical nexus and forward staging ground for the orcs defying Thrall's Horde and resisting the nearby reach of Stormwind.

sections.title: The Monument to Lothar
sections.body: Dominating the encampment is a massive stone statue of Lord Anduin Lothar, sword held high and pointing resolutely toward Blackrock Spire. Constructed shortly after the climax of the Second War, the monument marks the field where Lothar fell in battle against Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. In a bitter irony orchestrated by General Turalyon, defeated orc captives were forced into hard labor to raise the effigy of their greatest enemy. Curiously, despite holding the surrounding grounds today, the Dark Horde leaves the stone hero undisturbed amidst their crude huts.

faq.q: Why is there a giant statue of an Alliance hero inside an orc camp?
faq.answer: The statue honors Lord Anduin Lothar on the plain where he fell during the Second War's Siege of Blackrock Spire. Turalyon and the victorious Alliance forced captive orcs to quarry and raise the stone likeness. Years later, the Dark Horde reclaimed the land and built their camp directly around it.

faq.q: Why haven't the Blackrock orcs destroyed the statue?
faq.answer: The orcs of Black Tooth Hovel simply ignore the stone effigy. Breaking down such a colossal stone structure would consume immense time and resources for no practical gain, and some speculate the orcs still harbor a warrior's grudging respect for the commander who nearly broke them.

faq.q: Who lives in Black Tooth Hovel?
faq.answer: The encampment is manned by members of the Dark Horde: orcs of the Blackrock clan, allied Firegut ogres, and Smolderthorn forest trolls, alongside war kodos used to haul supplies.

faq.q: How did this camp get its name?
faq.answer: The camp is named after the Black Tooth Grin clan, a splinter faction originally formed by the sons of Blackhand that fought fiercely during the First and Second Wars.

angles.text: Beholding Lord Lothar's statue surrounded by brutal orcish huts is an infuriating reminder of how close the Dark Horde remains to the borders of the kingdom he gave his life to protect.
The renegade orcs camped beneath Lothar's stone gaze belong to the Dark Horde, rejecting Thrall's new vision in favor of old hatreds and black blood.
